findings.claim: Compose commits local PostgreSQL credentials, a JWT signing secret, and a database URL containing credentials.
The documented normal POC startup requires a pre-existing external dtf-netwok; neither Compose nor the POC harness provisions it, so service startup fails when that network is absent.
Four access-mutation hooks repeat the same workspace-access query invalidation branch; only the mutation function differs.
Direct-user and group-grant submit callbacks duplicate the same notice-reset, mutation, success-notice, and error-notice control flow.
The idempotency retention business duration is embedded as 24 hours in executor construction rather than represented by a named policy value.
Direct cross-origin clients that send Idempotency-Key need an allowed CORS header, but the documented POC UI uses same-origin /api Vite proxy and does not exercise this direct cross-origin path.
